- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next period; cap forecast at +3–4% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 3–5 days of forecast) — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term momentum.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative, model often fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overreacting to sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day horizon, model overpredicts in high-sentiment periods; apply a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment >0.75 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out — no correction needed unless price deviates >2% from 14-day moving average.
